name: @argszero/dsh-ptc-subcall-guard
description: Keeps a repeated PTC sub-call id out of the durable session log. deepseek-harness mints a `run_code` sub-call id as `<callId>:ptc:<n>` with `n` counted per execution, so a re-issued tool call numbers from 1 again under the same parent id. The write path accepts the repeat; the uniqueness requirement lives in the Session v4 format validator (`session-format-v3-to-v4/src/relationships.ts`, "PTC dispatch repeats subCallId") and is reached only when the whole log is next read, where reading is all-or-nothing. One repeat therefore costs the entire session: discussion #9677 reports a real 3,569-event session made permanently unopenable. This plugin shadows the `sessionPersistence` service instance's `open` and `create` — one own-property write, because both are prototype methods — and on the write handle each returns it renames a colliding `subCallId` to a session-unique one before the batch is appended, carrying the paired settle through a FIFO keyed by the original id, and priming the used-id set from the prefix the resume path already reads. The log it writes stays complete and loadable; the rename keeps `rootCallId`, so a nested dispatch's parent lookup still resolves. Zero runtime dependencies.
